knowledge_point.title: Solving a System of Equations by Eliminating the First Variable

question.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(x,y)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4x-4y &=-20 \\ 2x+5y &=-3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $x.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the $x$-coefficient in the first equation is $4,$ while in the second equation it is $2.$ 

If we multiply the second equation by $-2,$ then the $x$-coefficient will become $-4,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $4$ in the first equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}&4x-4y=-20 \\ &\left(2x+5y=-3\right)\times (-2)\end{aligned}\right.\;\Longrightarrow\;\left\{\begin{aligned}4x-4y &=-20 \\ -4x-10y &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $x$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\cancel{4x}-4y & =-20 \\ -\cancel{4x}-10y & =6 \\ (-4y-10y) & =(-20+6) \\ -14y & =-14 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $y=1.$ However, we still need to find $x.$ To do this, we substitute $y=1$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}2x+5y & =-3 \\ 2x+5(1) & =-3 \\ 2x+5 & =-3 \\ 2x & =-8 \\ x & =-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-4,\,y=1,$ which can be expressed as $(-4,1).$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the coefficient of $x$ in the  first  equation is $2,$ while in the second equation it is $4.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $-2,$ then the $x$-coefficient will become $-4,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $4$ in the second equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}&\left(2x-7y=26\right)\times (-2) \\ &4x-4y=12\end{aligned}\right.\;\Longrightarrow\;\left\{\begin{aligned}-4x+14y &=-52 \\ 4x-4y &=12\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $x$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\cancel{4x}+14y & =-52 \\ \cancel{4x}-4y & =12 \\ (14y-4y) & =(-52+12) \\ 10y & =-40 \\ y & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $y=-4.$ However, we still need to find $x.$ To do this, we substitute $y=-4$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-7y & =26 \\ 2x-7(-4) & =26 \\ 2x+28 & =26 \\ 2x & =-2 \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-1,\,y=-4,$ which can be expressed as $(-1,-4).$

question.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(u,v)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2u-v &=-5 \\ 4u+4v &=8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $u.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the $u$-coefficient in the first equation is $-2,$ while in the second equation it is $4.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $2,$ then the $u$-coefficient will become $-4,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $4$ in the second equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}&\left(-2u-v=-5\right)\times (2) \\ &4u+4v=8\end{aligned}\right.\;\Longrightarrow\;\left\{\begin{aligned}-4u-2v &=-10 \\ 4u+4v &=8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $u$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-\cancel{4u}-2v & =-10 \\ \cancel{4u}+4v & =8 \\ (-2v+4v) & =(-10+8) \\ 2v & =-2 \\ v & =-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $v=-1.$ However, we still need to find $u.$ To do this, we substitute $v=-1$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-2u-v & =-5 \\ -2u-(-1) & =-5 \\ -2u+1 & =-5 \\ -2u & =-6 \\ u & =3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=3,\,v=-1,$ which can be expressed as $(3,-1).$
